primitives.name: Integer Programming Formulation
primitives.verbatim_quote: Method / model - IP: max Z = Σj cjxj + Σj cjyj (captain doubles); constraints: Σx = 11, Σvjxj ≤ 83.5 (budget net of reserves), Σy = 1, y ≤ x, position min/max, ≤3 players per real team.
primitives.latex: \max_{x,y} \sum_j c_j x_j + \sum_j c_j y_j \quad \text{s.t.} \quad \sum_j x_j = 11, \sum_j v_j x_j \leq 83.5, \sum_j y_j = 1, y \leq x, \text{pos. bounds}, \sum_{i \in T} x_i \leq 3 \forall T
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'Z': 'Total expected points (dimensionless)', 'c_j': 'Expected points for player j (points)', 'x_j': 'Binary variable indicating player j selected (dimensionless)', 'y_j': 'Binary variable indicating captaincy of player j (dimensionless)', 'v_j': 'Value (salary) of player j (currency)', 'T': 'Real team identifier (dimensionless)'}
primitives.assumptions: Players' expected points are independent; budget constraint is fixed at 83.5; no stacking or covariance considered.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When player data is incomplete or missing, the model fails to converge.

layer2.mapping: The integer program mirrors GSE's lineup optimization kernel, where x and y represent active and captain selections respectively, while constraints reflect resource and positional limits.
layer2.telemetry: Lineup score vs baseline naive selection

primitives.name: Robust Min-Max Optimization
primitives.verbatim_quote: - Robust: box uncertainty U = {cj ∈ [c̄j-dj, c̄j+dj]}; max_{x,y} min_{c∈U} Σ cj(xj+yj).
primitives.latex: \max_{x,y} \min_{c \in U} \sum_j c_j (x_j + y_j) \quad \text{where} \quad U = \{c_j \in [\bar{c}_j - d_j, \bar{c}_j + d_j]\}
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'U': 'Uncertainty set for cost coefficients (points)', 'c_j': 'Estimated expected points for player j (points)', 'd_j': 'Deviation bound around estimate (points)', '\\bar{c}_j': 'Nominal estimate of expected points (points)'}
primitives.assumptions: Cost estimates lie within bounded intervals; worst-case scenario is used for conservative planning.
primitives.breakdown_regime: In high-variance environments, worst-case analysis may overly penalize optimistic strategies.

layer2.mapping: This formulation enables GSI to compute risk-adjusted predictions by evaluating performance under adversarial perturbations of input estimates.

primitives.name: Predictive Modeling Benchmark
primitives.verbatim_quote: - Cost estimators compared: simple average; linear-weighted average (wi = i/Σj); Holt-Winters additive trend; empirical bootstrap; Monte Carlo; ARIMA(p,d,q); linear trend regression; hybrid (Ridge on non-scoring features via SHAP, blended 2:1 actual:predicted); alternative objectives (ICT index, EGI - EGC).
primitives.assumptions: Historical point data suffices for forecasting; model accuracy improves with richer feature sets.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Models fail when underlying patterns shift unexpectedly or when new variables emerge.

layer2.mapping: Each estimator corresponds to a GSE feature-engineering pipeline component, mapping historical data into probabilistic forecasts for lineup construction.

reasoning_traces.think:
The core mathematical structure of the fantasy lineup problem is an integer program with binary decision variables representing player inclusion and captaincy. The objective function maximizes total expected points subject to constraints on budget, roster composition, and team diversity. This formulation aligns with standard combinatorial optimization problems. The robust variant introduces a min-max framework to hedge against uncertainty in point estimates, which is modeled as a box uncertainty set. While this approach provides theoretical resilience, empirical results suggest it underperforms in practice due to over-conservatism. Predictive modeling benchmarks compare various statistical techniques to generate cost vectors, including simple averaging, time-series models like Holt-Winters and ARIMA, and machine learning hybrids. These methods vary in complexity and fidelity to observed trends but share the common goal of estimating player contribution accurately. The assumption of independence among players' performances simplifies computation but omits strategic interactions such as stacking or defensive strength correlations. Failure modes include data gaps leading to infeasible solutions and model drift causing degraded forecast quality.
